newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends down on end of day RBI dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends down on end of day RBI dlr buying.

text.p: The spot rupee ended down at 35.78/79 against the dollar on Thursday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) hit leading banks with buy orders minutes before the market closed, dealers said.
The had opened the day steady at 35.76/77. Most of the day's deals were at 35.76, they said.
"They showed up around 2 o'clock in the afternoon," said a bank dealer referring to the RBI. His bank sold dollars to the RBI at the 35.78 level, he said.
"They seem to be defending the 35.75 mark," said a dealer.
The forward premiums rose by about two paise on purchases by the Industrial Development Bank but eased by a paisa later, in tandem with the easing of call rates, dealers said.
"Some banks were also reversing their earlier positions today," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The six-month annualised premium closed Thursday at 4.36 percent compared to the previous close of 4.19 percent.
"According to our calculations and that of J.P. Morgan, the rupee is overvalued by 10 percent compared to the real effective exchange rate (REER)," a dealer at a European bank said.
He said an RBI official told a forex conference last year that the central bank wanted REER parity in the medium term.
Some dealers said the 10 percent year-on-year fall in Indian exports in April was the first sign that an overvalued rupee was beginning to hurt the country's competitiveness.
An official of Arvind Mills, a leading export firm, told Reuters on Thursday an overvalued rupee was among the important factors that made exports less attractive to Indian firms.
